title: Val Thorens ski pass prices 2026/27: official rates and which to buy
metaTitle: Val Thorens ski pass prices 2026/27: official rates | SkiShare
description: Official 2026/27 Val Thorens lift pass prices: €367.50 for 6 days, €421 for the 3 Vallées, day and child rates, Family Flex, cheaper early-season dates.
keywords: how much is a ski pass in val thorens
intro: An adult 6-day lift pass costs **€367.50 for Val Thorens-Orelle** and **€421 for the whole of Les 3 Vallées** from 19 December 2026, according to the official 2026/27 price list of SETAM, the Val Thorens lift company. Until 18 December they cost €330.50 and €378.50 (Les 3 Vallées opens on 5 December), and the 3 Vallées pass drops back to €378.50 from 10 to 18 April 2027. A main-season day pass costs €73.50 for Val Thorens-Orelle or €84.20 for the 3 Vallées, and children under 5 ski free.

sections.heading: When is the Val Thorens lift pass cheaper in 2026/27?
paragraphs: The pass is cheaper from 21 November to 18 December 2026 for Val Thorens-Orelle, and from 5 to 18 December and 10 to 18 April 2027 for the 3 Vallées. Val Thorens-Orelle has no late-season rate.

Snow and crowds week by week: [when to ski in Val Thorens](/en/guide/best-time-to-ski-in-val-thorens).

sections.heading: How much is a day pass in Val Thorens?
paragraphs: An adult day pass costs €73.50 for Val Thorens-Orelle and €84.20 for the 3 Vallées from 19 December 2026, and €66.10 and €75.70 at the early rate:
after: Passes of 2 to 4 days cost the day price times the number of days, so there is no saving below six days.

**Saturday, online only:** bought by 11.59pm on Friday, the adult day pass costs €66.10 instead of €73.50 at Val Thorens-Orelle and €67.30 instead of €84.20 for the 3 Vallées (prices from 19 December 2026). On a Saturday, the whole of Les 3 Vallées then costs just €1.20 more than Val Thorens-Orelle.

sections.heading: How much is a 6-day ski pass in Val Thorens?
paragraphs: An adult 6-day pass costs €367.50 for Val Thorens-Orelle and €421 for the 3 Vallées from 19 December 2026, because every 6-day pass is sold at the price of five days:
after: The list has no 5-day pass, only ‘5 days + 1 free’: if you plan five days, the sixth is free. Days run consecutively, rest days included. Beyond six days, each extra main-season day adds €54 to an adult pass at Val Thorens-Orelle and €65 for the 3 Vallées, up to 15 days.

sections.heading: Val Thorens-Orelle or 3 Vallées: which pass should you buy?
paragraphs: Take the Val Thorens-Orelle pass to ski around Val Thorens all week, and the 3 Vallées pass for even one day in Les Menuires, Méribel or Courchevel. In the main season the difference is €53.50 for an adult week.
list: **Val Thorens-Orelle:** 150 km of pistes around Val Thorens and Orelle.
**Les 3 Vallées:** about 600 km, adding Les Menuires, Saint-Martin-de-Belleville, Méribel and Courchevel.

**One day elsewhere:** with a Val Thorens-Orelle pass of 2 days or more, a one-day 3 Vallées extension costs €51 (€41.80 for a junior) according to the Val Thorens tourist office; it is sold only at the ticket offices on the morning itself, if the weather and the links allow. A main-season week plus one extension (€367.50 + €51 = €418.50) is just €2.50 cheaper than the 3 Vallées pass.
**Early December:** the gap falls to €48 (€330.50 against €378.50), and a week plus one extension (€381.50) costs more than the 3 Vallées pass.
**Week of 10 April:** the 3 Vallées pass costs €378.50 and Val Thorens-Orelle €367.50, only €11 apart.
after: The extension’s rules and prices: [Val Thorens tourist office](https://www.valthorens.com/en/ski/forfaits/forfait-6-jours/). Which part of the village suits you: [where to stay in Val Thorens](/en/guide/where-to-stay-in-val-thorens).

sections.heading: Children, seniors and Family Flex: who pays less?
paragraphs: Children under 5 ski free, juniors aged 5 to 17 pay about 18% less than adults and veterans aged 75 and over about a quarter of the adult price. Day and week passes have no age reduction from 18 to 74, and the list has no student rate.
list: **Under 5:** free, collected at a SETAM ticket office with official proof of age, such as a passport, and a recent photo (SETAM can take one by webcam).
**Junior, 5 to 17:** on proof of date of birth. The age that counts is the age on the pass’s first day.
**Veteran, 75 and over:** ticket offices only, with ID and a photo.

**Family Flex:** the whole group pays the junior rate on passes of 6 to 21 days: at least 3 people, with one or two adults (18 to 74) and one to six children (5 to 17), the same area and length for all, one payment. A main-season week then costs €301 each for Val Thorens-Orelle and €345 for the 3 Vallées (€271 and €310 at the early rates). Les 3 Vallées’ own page offers it from 5 days, at the same €345.
**Under 30:** the ‘-30 ans’ rate (30% off) is for season passes only.

**Disability:** a reduced rate on valid proof. French residents show a Carte Mobilité Inclusion marked ‘invalidité’, ‘priorité’ or ‘station debout pénible’; residents of other countries need an official document from their country of residence, in French or with an official translation.

sections.heading: Where can you buy a Val Thorens lift pass?
paragraphs: SETAM, the Val Thorens lift company, sells passes online at [ski.valthorens.com](https://ski.valthorens.com/en/home/) and at its ticket offices and machines in the resort. SkiShare does not sell lift passes on this site.
list: **Online:** free delivery by post if you order at least 10 days before your first day (SETAM does not post to the USA), collection from a resort machine with the code SETAM emails you, or reloading a card you already have (numbers starting 01-1614). You can order the last two up to the last minute.

**Ticket offices:** Forum, Funitel Péclet and Cairn/Caron/P4 open daily, Olympiades from Saturday to Monday and Montana at weekends. On Saturdays Olympiades, Forum and Montana open from 8.45am to 7pm.

**Machines** for buying, collecting and reloading: 7am to 11pm at Olympiades, Forum and Montana, 24 hours a day at car park P2 and the bus station, and during the day at Funitel Péclet, Cairn/Caron/P4 and the tourist office.
**Ticket office only:** free under-5 passes, veteran passes, the 3 Vallées extension and the EasyRider beginner pass.
**Payment:** cards, cash and ANCV holiday vouchers at the ticket offices; card online (SETAM’s site says PayPal is accepted from €1,000).
after: Keep the order email or receipt: with it, SETAM replaces a lost or stolen pass for the remaining days for €10. Unused passes bought online can be exchanged at a ticket office for other dates or another area.

You pay for piste rescue in Val Thorens. [Carré Neige](https://ski.valthorens.com/en/ski-insurance-carre-neige/) insurance, bought with the pass and for the same number of days, covers rescue, medical costs on top of your health insurance, and a refund of passes and lessons of more than 3 days after an accident or serious illness. SETAM lists it at €3.50 per person per day for 1 to 7 days and €28 for 8 to 21 days.

sections.heading: Beginners: free lifts and a half-price pass
paragraphs: Beginners can start for free on four covered carpet lifts (Campagnols, Musaraigne and the two Castor & Pollux carpets), then move to SETAM’s EasyRider pass at half the public price: €36.75 for an adult day from 19 December, €33.05 before.

EasyRider, for 4 hours or a day, opens five lifts (the Cairn, 2 Lacs and Caron gondolas and the Cascades and Moutière chairlifts) and the green and blue runs they serve. A junior day costs €30.10 (€27.10 before 19 December). It is sold only at the ticket offices.

Children in ESF’s ski kindergarten (the Piou-Piou and Sifflote classes) need no pass, according to [ESF Val Thorens](https://www.ski-school-valthorens.co.uk/advice/choose-a-ski-pass/). Once they ski on the pistes, they do.

faqs.q: How much is a ski pass in Val Thorens for 2026/27?
faqs.a: From 19 December 2026 an adult day pass costs €73.50 for Val Thorens-Orelle and €84.20 for the 3 Vallées, and a 6-day pass €367.50 and €421, according to SETAM. Until 18 December, Val Thorens-Orelle costs €66.10 a day and €330.50 for 6 days.

faqs.q: Is the 3 Vallées lift pass worth the extra?
faqs.a: It costs €53.50 more than Val Thorens-Orelle for a main-season adult week. If you want even one day in Méribel or Courchevel, it is only €2.50 more than a Val Thorens-Orelle week plus a one-day extension at €51, sold at the ticket offices on the morning itself if the links are open.

faqs.q: Do children ski free in Val Thorens?
faqs.a: Children under 5 do, with a free pass collected at a SETAM ticket office on proof of age. Juniors aged 5 to 17 pay a reduced rate, such as €301 for a main-season week at Val Thorens-Orelle.

faqs.q: What is the Family Flex pass?
faqs.a: A deal in which a group of at least 3 people, one or two adults and one to six children aged 5 to 17, all pay the junior rate on passes of 6 to 21 days. A main-season week then costs €301 each at Val Thorens-Orelle and €345 for the 3 Vallées.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to buy a Val Thorens lift pass online?
faqs.a: Only with SETAM’s web-only offers: standard passes cost the list price online too, but the adult Saturday day pass costs €67.30 instead of €84.20 for the 3 Vallées if bought by 11.59pm on Friday. Buying online also lets you go straight to the lifts.

faqs.q: Can I buy my lift pass from SkiShare?
faqs.a: No. On this site SkiShare rents apartments only. Lift passes are sold by SETAM, the Val Thorens lift company, online at ski.valthorens.com and in the resort.
